_about: Which traveller is the organizer, when the name was written in a different alphabet from the roster.
Read by BOTH sides so they cannot drift: control-plane/api/src/organizer-identity.ts (the interview, which
records the roster's own spelling or asks again) and control-plane/worker/control_plane_worker/transformer.py
(the build, which must find the same person). A case added here is enforced in both.
alike / not_alike: two names, compared by their consonants only, and only across alphabets.
resolve: a roster (the travelers answer) and what the organizer wrote; expect is the roster index, or null.

resolve.why: every roster name only in English letters, the organizer answered in Hebrew
a Hebrew-only roster, answered in English
two travellers sound alike, so nobody is picked
one consonant is too little to tell people apart
a different name in the same alphabet is a different name, not a spelling
an exact match wins before sound-alike is ever tried
the name is read from the front of a sentence first
a family name names a household, not a person, in any alphabet
